transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been struggling with severe sleep issues for nearly two years now, about a year and nine months to be exact. It has been incredibly exhausting because I just can't seem to get any restful sleep. I'm really hoping to find some help for this.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood, such as feelings of sadness, hopelessness, or irritability, alongside your sleep issues?

I haven't really felt sad or hopeless, but I have been incredibly irritable and easily annoyed. I find myself snapping at small things and have almost no patience for minor inconveniences that I'd normally just ignore. It feels like my fuse is just so short, especially since my sleep has been so poor.
Have you experienced any significant life changes or stressful events around the time your sleep issues and irritability started, about a year and nine months ago?

I don't recall any specific major life changes or stressful events happening around that time. However, I can definitely confirm that both my sleep issues and this constant irritability started right around a year and nine months ago.
Have your sleep issues and irritability been constant since they started, or have you noticed any periods where they improved or worsened over the past year and nine months?

I'm not really sure if there have been specific periods where things got better or worse. For the most part, both the sleep issues and my irritability have just been constant and persistent throughout the entire year and nine months.
Do you often find yourself worrying excessively about everyday things, even when there's no apparent reason to worry, and does this worry interfere with your daily life?

Yes, I worry constantly about everyday things like work, family, and finances, and I just can't seem to control it. It has been going on for about a year and nine months now, and these thoughts frequently intrude and make it really hard to focus on my daily tasks.

Has your ability to enjoy activities you once found pleasurable, such as hobbies or spending time with friends and family, been affected by your worries or irritability over the past year and nine months?

I haven't really noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in my hobbies or spending time with others. My main struggles are still just the constant worry, irritability, and sleep issues that I've been experiencing. Those are the things that are really wearing me down.
Can you describe more about these worries, are they focused on specific things like fear of the future, health concerns, or are they more free-floating and unpredictable?

My worries aren't focused on just one specific thing; they are free-floating and spread across almost every area of my life, like work, family, and finances. I also feel constantly trapped in "what if" questions because I find it incredibly hard to handle any uncertainty about the future.

For how long have you been experiencing these free-floating worries and 'what if' questions, and have you noticed any physical symptoms such as restlessness, feeling on edge, or difficulty concentrating, accompanying your worries?

I have been dealing with these constant worries and "what if" questions for the entire year and nine months. Along with that, I constantly feel restless, on edge, and wound up like a spring, which makes it incredibly difficult to focus or concentrate on my daily tasks.

So, just to confirm, you've been experiencing excessive and persistent worry about everyday things, restlessness, feeling on edge, and difficulty concentrating for about a year and nine months, is that correct?

Yes, that is exactly correct. I have been dealing with those constant, everyday worries, feeling wound up and on edge, and having trouble focusing for exactly about a year and nine months now. It has been a very persistent struggle for me.

It sounds like you've been experiencing many of the key symptoms of Generalized Anxiety Disorder, such as excessive and persistent worry, restlessness, and difficulty concentrating, for a significant period of time. Is there anything else you'd like to add or discuss before we consider a treatment plan for your anxiety?

Yes, that sounds accurate, but I really want to emphasize how severe my sleep issues are—I struggle to fall asleep, wake up constantly from nightmares, and always wake up feeling completely exhausted. On top of that, my body is constantly stiff and tense, and because my patience is totally depleted, I keep snapping at the people around me.
